questions.q: What question does the Open Account Balances Listing answer, as opposed to the Account Analysis Report?
options: It answers "what posted to this account historically," the same question as the Account Analysis Report
It answers "what is still outstanding right now," breaking a control account's balance into its unsettled items
It answers "what is the ledger's functional currency"
It answers "who has access to modify this account"
questions.explain: The Open Account Balances Listing focuses specifically on items that remain open, not the full historical activity that posted to an account.

questions.q: Why can't a plain GL account balance alone tell you which specific items are still outstanding?
options: Because GL account balances do not exist in Oracle Fusion
Because a plain balance is a single net total, and does not break down into the individual items that make it up
Because only Receivables has a balance at all
Because balances are recalculated randomly
questions.explain: A plain account balance is one net number; it cannot show, on its own, which individual items are open versus already settled.

questions.q: What makes the Open Account Balances Listing possible, according to this lesson?
options: Supporting references, like a supplier number, attached to journal lines hitting a shared control account
A description rule with no sources at all
The ledger's calendar setup
Deleting the account segment entirely
questions.explain: Supporting reference data (such as supplier number) lets the report attribute open balances back to specific suppliers or invoices.

questions.q: In the worked example, what did the Open Account Balances Listing for AP Trade show?
options: A single undifferentiated total of $45,000 with no detail
Specific open invoices, such as INV-2201 from Meridian Supply Co. for $12,000, adding up to the account's $45,000 balance
A list of every supplier the company has ever worked with, regardless of balance
Only paid invoices, with no mention of open ones
questions.explain: The example broke the $45,000 AP Trade balance down into specific still-open invoices by supplier, which sum to the total balance.

questions.q: For which type of account is an Open Account Balances Listing most commonly used?
options: A fixed asset depreciation expense account
A third-party control account, such as Accounts Payable Trade or Accounts Receivable, representing a combined balance across many parties
A bank reconciliation clearing account used only once a year
A tax-exempt revenue account
questions.explain: Control accounts like AP Trade or AR, which combine balances across many suppliers or customers, are the primary use case for this report.
